observable: the electron and ion integrated-moment histories, the field energy and the final emitted-electron boundary frame
variant: ic/variant/value.txt changes n0 from 1.0e17 to 1.0000000000000003e17, exactly two upward binary64 ULP.

warrant: The graded histories and frames follow the emission boundary condition (`GKYL_SPECIES_EMISSION` with an emission spectrum model), the boundary-flux source and non-periodic Poisson boundary conditions. In `rt_vlasov_poisson_emission_spectrum_1x1v_p2.c`, `n0` (line 129) is the reference density of both species; the two-ULP variant therefore moves every graded value at the level of the arithmetic, while a wrong emission yield, a wrong boundary-flux accounting or a wrong Poisson boundary changes them at order one. The bound atol=1e-09, rtol=1e-09 was set on 2026-09-06 from the calibration selfcheck on the x86 worker 136.114.2.6 (1 cpu, 4 GB, Docker): the two-ULP variant used at most 6.0e-3 of it and the strict-IEEE altbuild at most 3.9e-3 (worst files `elc-imom.gkyl` and `ion-imom.gkyl`), a headroom of about 168x over the larger legitimate perturbation, while the faults named above move the graded values at order one. Component overrides: `elc-imom.gkyl` (3 values per sample) component 1 atol=1e+10, rtol=1e-09; `ion-imom.gkyl` (3 values per sample) component 1 atol=1e+06, rtol=1e-09. Those components are cancellation residuals or near-zero moments (here the parallel momenta of a sheath whose net flow starts at zero): their absolute spread under the two legitimate perturbations sits far above the file-level bound while their scale is orders of magnitude below the other components of the same history, so each keeps its own decade-rounded bound at the same 100x rule and stays fully graded.
